<research_package>

## Research question
How do Wickersham-MT's gains from pivot-filtered back-translation compare with the improvement previously reported for the technique?

## Methods summary
Wickersham-MT is a 240M-parameter Transformer translation model trained separately for four English→X low-resource pairs. We add synthetic parallel data produced by pivot-filtered back-translation, which back-translates monolingual target-language text into English and keeps only sentence pairs whose round trip through a pivot language scores above a threshold. The technique is commonly credited to Ambergate & Toivonen (2022), who are often cited for a gain of about 6 BLEU on low-resource pairs.

## Experimental setup
Four English→X pairs are studied: Nepali (en→ne), Sinhala (en→si), Khmer (en→km) and Pashto (en→ps). Genuine parallel data come from the Fenmoor-Parl corpus; monolingual target-language text for back-translation comes from news crawls. Systems are evaluated on Fenmoor-Test (1,012 sentences per pair) with BLEU and chrF computed by the same detokenised scoring script. Each configuration was trained once (single run); the default pivot round-trip threshold is 0.4.

## Experiments and comparisons
- `exp1`: Effect of synthetic parallel data
  - comparison `exp1/cmp1`: Pivot-filtered back-translation vs genuine parallel data only, BLEU and chrF per pair
  - comparison `exp1/cmp2`: Pivot-filtered vs unfiltered back-translation, BLEU and chrF per pair
- `exp2`: Pivot round-trip threshold ablation
  - comparison `exp2/cmp3`: Thresholds 0.2, 0.4 and 0.6: synthetic pairs kept and average BLEU
- `exp3`: External comparison
  - comparison `exp3/cmp4`: Wickersham-MT with pivot-filtered back-translation vs Pellston-NMT, BLEU per pair

## Cited source passages
- `P1` — Ambergate & Toivonen (2022), "Round-Trip Filtering for Synthetic Parallel Data":
  > For all systems in Section 5 we generated 2.1M synthetic sentence pairs with pivot-filtered back-translation, discarding candidates whose round-trip score through the pivot language fell below 0.4, and appended them to the genuine parallel data. Section 6 analyses which sentence types the filter removes.
- `P2` — Rasmussen-Obi & Petrakis (2023), "Synthetic Data for Low-Resource Translation: A Controlled Comparison":
  > Relative to systems trained on genuine parallel data alone, adding pivot-filtered back-translation improved BLEU by 5.8 points on average across our four low-resource pairs, compared with 2.9 points for unfiltered back-translation.
- `P3` — Iwu-Castellanos et al. (2021), "Fenmoor-Parl: Parliamentary Proceedings for Low-Resource Translation":
  > Fenmoor-Parl aligns between 180k and 620k sentence pairs per language from regional parliamentary records; the Fenmoor-Test sets were translated from scratch by professional translators and contain 1,012 sentences per pair.
- `P4` — Oyelaran & Brisk (2020), "Reporting chrF for Morphologically Rich Targets":
  > Character n-gram F-score correlated more strongly with human adequacy judgements than BLEU for the agglutinative target languages in our study.

## Task
Write a short Results/Discussion passage (2–4 sentences) that answers the research question using only the evidence in this package.

sentences.text: Adding pivot-filtered back-translation to Wickersham-MT improved average BLEU by 3.1 points over genuine parallel data alone (from 12.0 to 15.1) across the four low-resource pairs, a smaller gain than the 5.8-point average improvement previously reported for the technique by Rasmussen-Obi & Petrakis (2023).
Pivot-filtered back-translation also outperformed unfiltered back-translation on average BLEU (15.1 vs 13.4) and average chrF (42.3 vs 40.3), with gains on every individual pair for both metrics.

The default pivot round-trip threshold of 0.4 yielded the highest average BLEU (15.1) among the three thresholds tested (0.2: 14.3; 0.6: 14.8), while the number of synthetic pairs kept decreased as the threshold increased (3.0M, 1.8M, 1.1M).

Wickersham-MT with pivot-filtered back-translation achieved a higher average BLEU (15.1) than the external Pellston-NMT system (14.5) across the four pairs, though Pellston-NMT scored higher on en→si (15.0 vs 14.2).
